comment: Coding-backend bundle manifest. See docs/EXTENDING.md for how backends are selected. v2 (2026-05-04 reconciliation) adds 'distribution' (npm | github_release) + 'npm_package' for npm-distributed CLIs (Cline, Continue, Claude SDK, Gemini CLI). Versions and sha256 placeholders are filled in by scripts/build-coding-cli-manifest.sh at release-build time. Do NOT hand-edit shipped manifests; edit the build helper instead.

opencode.comment: Was marked bundled:true pointing at a directory NO build ever staged — the entry listed as '(bundled)' while a clean install had nothing, and an unguarded registration meant it registered anyway and failed at task time (found live on the household node 2026-08-27). Real distribution is npm; the adapter itself is unchanged.

goose.comment: Repo moved block/goose -> aaif-goose/goose under AAIF/Linux Foundation. Asset naming uses Rust target triples; Windows uses .zip upstream — build helper substitutes per-platform suffix. Provider auth: NOT GOOSE_PROVIDER_KEY (wyrdsekai invention); upstream Goose reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY / GOOGLE_API_KEY directly per provider. Adapter maps coding.backends.goose.provider -> correct env var.

api_key.note: Per-provider: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY / GOOGLE_API_KEY / (none for local). Adapter sets the right env var based on coding.backends.goose.provider; no GOOSE_PROVIDER_KEY indirection.

codezaiku.comment: BUNDLED DEFAULT as of 0.2.0. CodeZaiku (was CodePlane) - Apache-2.0, Wyrdsekai/codezaiku. ONE platform-independent tarball because it is a JVM app, so there is no per-platform asset and every platform key carries the SAME sha - the one artifact named five times, because the installer keys on <platform>-<arch> and has no platform-independent key. It ships bin/codezaiku and bin/codezaiku.bat, so all five are genuinely supported. Needs a JRE 21+; the .deb declares that dependency and the tarball does not, which is why the upstream installer points apt users at the .deb. Its own installer defaults to a PER-USER prefix (~/.local), so the binary often sits outside a service PATH - BackendExecutableResolver searches the data-dir owner's home for exactly this reason. Model routing travels only via CODEZAIKU_DRIVE / CODEZAIKU_MODEL, which the adapter sets from the node's own inference endpoint like every other backend. The download_url/sha are not dead weight on a bundled entry: packaging/build-dist.sh fetches and verifies against THEM to stage the bundle, so a release cannot ship a codezaiku that differs from what this manifest attests.

api_key.note: Only for a HOSTED drive. Against the household's own inference endpoint CodeZaiku needs no key; CODEZAIKU_AUTH_TOKEN is the Key Chest slot when it does.

pi.comment: pi.dev's pi-coding-agent (MIT). In the fallback chain and fully wired (PiCodingRuntimeConfig/PiCodingBackend) since Phase 2, but NEVER in this manifest — so auth resolution answered 'Backend pi not found in manifest' and every dispatch died as LOGIN_REQUIRED even against the local drive, which needs no login at all. A backend the chain can select must have a manifest row; the chain and the manifest were two lists nobody compared.

api_key.note: None against the household's local drive. Cloud providers read their own env keys (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY) per provider.

claude-sdk.comment: Distributed via npm @anthropic-ai/claude-code; reuses ClaudeCliInference.java pattern. Headless OAuth: claude login --no-browser (paste-this-URL device flow).

oauth.note: Points at the FILE, not a directory: the liveness check counts any non-empty directory as a session, and ~/.claude holds backups/projects on a box that has never logged in — a directory path here reports a session that does not exist, and the child then fails interactively. The old value ~/.config/claude/ was a location no Claude Code version ever wrote. claude login --no-browser is the headless paste-this-URL OAuth flow (code.claude.com/docs/en/headless). Pre-2026-05 the manifest mistakenly marked this false. Existing pattern in core/src/main/java/org/wyrdsekai/core/inference/ClaudeCliInference.java.

gemini-cli.min_version_reason: CVSS-10 RCE; original patches in 0.39.1 / 0.40.0-preview.3, cherry-pick floor v0.40.1 (2026-04-30)

oauth.note: Headless paste-this-URL OAuth EXISTS: NO_BROWSER=true triggers getOauthConsentNonInteractive (verified in the shipped 0.57.0 bundle). An earlier note claimed no headless flow; it described an older release.

cline.comment: Distributed via npm `cline` (cline.bot/blog/announcing-cline-cli-2-0). GitHub releases publish only the .vsix IDE extension. Headless argv: cline -y "<task>" or cline --json "<task>" with prompt as POSITIONAL.

oauth.note: Browser OAuth via `cline auth` with no args; credential file location is not publicly documented as of May 2026.

api_key.note: Pre-stage credentials via `cline auth -p <provider> -k <key>` OR set the standard provider env var (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY / etc.) — Cline reads them directly. CLINE_PROVIDER_KEY is wyrdsekai's invention and is no longer used.

continue.comment: Distributed via npm @continuedev/cli; binary name `cn`; requires Node.js 20+. Headless argv: cn -p "<prompt>" with prompt as POSITIONAL. Source: docs.continue.dev/cli/quickstart + docs.continue.dev/guides/cli.

oauth.note: First run prompts browser OAuth; no dedicated `cn login` subcommand in current upstream docs (May 2026). Headless hosts can use CONTINUE_API_KEY env var instead.

openhands.comment: The pinned runtime tag v1.7.0 no longer exists on ghcr - upstream PRUNES version tags (GitHub releases at v1.15.0, registry holds only 0.x relics plus latest), so any hard image pin here rots. `latest` is the only stable name for the legacy sandbox image. The ADAPTER's real dependency is the V1 agent-server (pip install openhands-agent-server, REST+WS on :8000); the docker image is a legacy convenience only. Targets V1 Agent Server (OpenHands/software-agent-sdk v1.20.0 May 4 2026). Adapter speaks REST + WebSocket to `openhands-agent-server --port 8000`, NOT JSON-RPC MCP (the MCP shape used pre-2026-05-04 was fabricated). Docker-image tag is the legacy OpenHands/OpenHands runtime image (v1.7.0); V1 SDK Agent Server is typically run via pip install openhands-agent-server, but the docker_image is retained for `wyrd setup openhands` users who want the legacy runtime sandbox.
